Pengxi Liu

I am a Ph.D. student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at Duke University. My research focuses on diffusion-based generative models, spanning theoretical foundations (e.g., trajectory-level optimization of diffusion dynamics) and applications in diffusion language models and efficient, controllable image and video generation.

Before Duke, I received my master's degree from ETH Zurich and my bachelor's degree from Zhejiang University.

Selected Research

I study how diffusion trajectories, prediction targets, and model architectures affect generation quality and efficiency. My earlier work explored distributional alignment through optimal transport.

  • Variational Trajectory Optimization of Anisotropic Diffusion Schedules
    Pengxi Liu*, Zeyu Michael Li*, Xiang Cheng
    Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2026 (accepted)
    paper/ code

    We jointly optimize the denoiser and a matrix-valued noise trajectory, allowing different subspaces to follow different schedules. An anisotropic ODE solver supports efficient sampling.

    * Equal contribution.
  • The Noise-Transmission Burden of Diffusion Network: Why Image Prediction Can Outperform Noise Prediction
    Gyeonghun Kang*, Pengxi Liu*, Bingshuo Qian*, Xiang Cheng
    In Submission
    arXiv

    We study why image and noise prediction behave differently in diffusion Transformers. Input compression creates a noise-transmission burden; analytic output preconditioning reduces the burden on the learned network.

    * Equal contribution.
  • Distributional Alignment via Proportional Optimal Transport
    Pengxi Liu, Yi Shen, Matthew M. Engelhard, Benjamin A. Goldstein, Michael J. Pencina, Nicoleta J. Economou-Zavlanos, Michael M. Zavlanos
    AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society (AIES), 2025
    paper/ arXiv

    We align score distributions by transporting a selected proportion of source scores, while keeping the reference distribution fixed. The transported proportion controls the trade-off between distributional alignment and ranking performance.
